newsitem.title: USA: Tennessee cuts deficit estimate to $70 million.
newsitem.headline: Tennessee cuts deficit estimate to $70 million.

text.p: Tennessee has reduced its estimated budget deficit for fiscal 1997 to $70 millioin, down from the $110 million previously expected for the year ending June 30.

Deputy Comptroller John Morgan told the House Finance Committee Tuesday that consumer spending has buoyed sales tax collections, helping shrink the size of the deficit in the state's $14 billion budget. Business strength has also boosted franchise and excise tax collections.

Morgan said the state's economy has slowed, though not as much as expected. Gov. Don Sunquist is expected to outline cost-cutting proposals when he presents his fiscal 1998 budget to the legislature on Monday.
